title: Weekly dance circuit and a Chicago trip
summary: Handy lists the week's dances after a lake day, and ends with a brief trip to Chicago with Albert Morgan.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, some of them. Some of them. Then some of them used to just jump in there for fun and get drunk like that. Just jump in the water. Close and watch everything. Load it, tennis. Jump overboard. I used to like to play out there. It used to get me to go to Moss Point, Mississippi. Play that Saturday night. We got to catch that first train out of there. Pass it through there around four something in the morning. Then you get in here around seven thirty something to eat. And we got to be out there at the lake at nine. To go scuffling in. No sleep. That's when you get to around two o'clock in the evening. Everybody's gone swimming and nobody in there. But got a couple old people sitting around there eating sandwiches or drinking or something like that. They don't want to dance. I mean, you get tired of just sitting there playing to the walls and that sleep coming down on you. But it's tough. Then you got to get up and walk around, go get some ice water, wash your face. Try to get yourself straight down. And the beatiness thing, then you have to go play it at the Caporato Hall at night. Oh man. Oh the economy hall. Oh man. And when you get there, the people in there like that. They want nothing but them old blues all night long. If they don't want the blues, you play something. You don't never play too fast for them. They ain't like it at night. You could play fast. You want that. That was one step for them. You used to play shotties, cakewalks, all those things. They have the prize for the best waltzer, and the prize for the best shotties dancer, prize for the best cakewalk dancer. Play all that play. Through the night of the dance. And then from there, on Monday night, they go to Pantitula. Another dance there. And then you might rest Tuesday night. Wednesday night, you go to Tibidó. Play a jitney dance there. So it's the night you go to Racelet. You play a jitney dance there. Friday night, we play at the Fryman's Hall in West Wego. Saturday night, we gone back to Moss Point Recipe or Gulfport, one of them places.
We used to play so much to attend the troops. Send somebody in our place sometimes.
Albert Morgan was playing baseball with us. Him and I were taking a vacation with Chicago. Just got tired of it. We stayed in Chicago a week. And come back. After we done got about broke. stuff
